Based on the retrieved matches, the answer to your question can be synthesized as follows:

Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) is not known to modify the frequency and topographic distribution of lymph node metastases (LNM) in patients with cervical cancer. However, clinical non-responders showed more involved LNs.

This means that while NACT may have some effect on the overall extent of lymphadenectomy required for patients treated with surgery, it does not significantly alter the distribution or frequency of lymph nodes that are involved by cancer cells. This is in contrast to patients who do not respond well to NACT, where more extensive lymph node dissections may be necessary.

Therefore, a systemic and extensive lymphadenectomy should still be performed in patients treated with NACT plus surgery regardless of the response to NACT, as it remains an essential part of the treatment protocol for these patients.
